title: Isolated worktrees for subagents leak stale untracked state across dispatches (dev-team skill)
details:
**What happened:** Two separate `programmer` subagent dispatches (isolation: worktree), each into a brand-new worktree directory named after a unique agent id, found pre-existing content in `.slice/red` and `.slice/red_files` (an ephemeral, gitignored state dir the dev-team skill's engine writes) referencing commits/files from an unrelated PRIOR run's slice with the same slice id (e.g. an old "S2" from a run that predates this session's `devteam init --force`). `.slice/id`/`.slice/mode`/`.slice/footprint` were correctly fresh each time, but `.slice/red*` was stale, causing the guard hook to wrongly report frozen-test violations and block all edits.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model. Both subagents independently diagnosed the issue correctly and stopped rather than working around it.
**Repro:** In a repo with `.claude/worktrees/` used across multiple dev-team runs/slice-id reuse (same slice id "S2" in two different `plan.md` runs), dispatch a fresh `programmer` agent with `isolation: worktree` for a slice id that was used in an earlier run. The new worktree directory's `.slice/red`/`.slice/red_files` (untracked, gitignored) already contain the OLD run's commit sha and file list.
**Evidence:** Session dir `/Users/yamazaki-ethan/Documents/Projects/Naga777/Stable_NAGAS_777/stable-be-naga-fortune-777`; worktrees `.claude/worktrees/agent-aa7706a57990dcd49` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-a9f5bb9814b0e0125`; stale references to commit `dd19bbee8` (unrelated file NagaCommandHandlerTest.java) and commit `52e1d0ea2` (an old S2 slice "RTP conformance: Naga Eye bet scaling...").
**Cause:** `devteam.py`'s `cmd_claim` only resets `.slice/red`/`.slice/red_files` inside its `mode == "green"` branch (to pre-populate them for a GREEN dispatch); a fresh RED-mode claim never clears them, and something in the worktree-provisioning layer (outside devteam.py, likely the harness's own isolation/worktree-pool mechanism) is not giving each dispatch a truly clean untracked-file state, so leftover `.slice/red*` from a completely different worktree occupant survives into a new agent's worktree.
